report.title: LoRa Network comprehensive Answer Engine Optimisation audit
report.scope: Repository, production build output, generated HTML, structured data, robots.txt, sitemap.xml, catalogue architecture, representative answer extraction, and current official crawler guidance.
changesMade: Created this report only. No routes, catalogue data, prices, page content, structured data, crawler rules, or application code were changed.
limitations: The audit assessed the production build locally. The live production hostname and deployment environment were not available, so production environment variables, edge/WAF rules, Search Console data, Bing Webmaster data, logs, and real index coverage could not be verified.

The in-app visual browser could not attach because its sandbox bootstrap failed. Rendered production HTML was inspected directly and dynamic comparison output was fetched from a local production server instead.
No external keyword-volume or competitor-audit tools were used, as requested.

executiveAeoScore.verdict: Sound technical catalogue foundation, but not yet a strong independent answer source. The site is readily crawlable and commercially consistent; its biggest constraints are generic product explanations, thin application and buying-guide content, incomplete entity/trust information, and a current build configured with localhost canonical URLs.

contentClarity.preventsHigherScore: Core facts are clearly labelled, but descriptions frequently repeat a generic application/interface sentence and raw comma-separated specifications instead of explaining the product in plain language.

entityClarity.preventsHigherScore: LoRa Network is visibly the reseller brand and Dragino is labelled as the brand, but there is no Organization entity, no explicit reseller/manufacturer relationship statement, and the current build contains no configured business contact identity.

productPageUsefulness.preventsHigherScore: SKU, application, interface, price and source specifications are present, but suitability, variant differences, structured specification rows, and model-specific guidance are often absent.

questionAnswerCoverage.preventsHigherScore: The catalogue answers availability questions well, but direct comparisons, suitability questions, technology trade-offs and selection questions are weak or missing.

structuredData.preventsHigherScore: All 981 product JSON-LD blocks parse and price integrity is excellent, but Organization is absent, facet breadcrumbs are not marked up, Article entities are minimal, and 981 largely repetitive FAQPage blocks add little search value.

internalLinking.preventsHigherScore: Products connect to valid applications, connectivity pages and related products, but only seven families and five broad guides provide comparison/guidance links; many obvious model ranges therefore have no family or comparison path.

crawlability.preventsHigherScore: Core facts are server-rendered, all product routes build statically, and wildcard robots access is open. The score is capped by unverified production WAF behaviour, client-side catalogue filtering, and the localhost URL fallback in the audited build.

indexationArchitecture.preventsHigherScore: The 1,027-URL sitemap is disciplined and compare is noindex, but every product page is indexable despite substantial template similarity, and the audited sitemap/canonicals point to localhost until production configuration is supplied.

topicalAuthority.preventsHigherScore: Catalogue breadth is high, yet educational depth is low: five short guides and six sourced connectivity explanations are not enough to establish strong authority across 981 industrial IoT products.

productComparisonUsefulness.preventsHigherScore: Tables are semantic and show useful factual fields and ZAR prices, but they reproduce raw specifications and do not synthesize the decisive differences or best-fit use cases.

southAfricanCommercialRelevance.preventsHigherScore: ZAR pricing, en-ZA metadata and South African positioning are clear, but fulfilment, VAT status, delivery, warranty, support and legal-business details remain deliberately unclaimed or unconfigured.

technicalAccessibility.preventsHigherScore: The site has a skip link, headings, definition lists and semantic tables. Nested main elements on legal pages, unlabeled breadcrumb navigation, and some mojibake reduce semantic and editorial quality.

sourceCredibility.preventsHigherScore: Connectivity claims cite LoRa Alliance or GSMA and the workbook is authoritative internally, but only 212 of 981 catalogue rows expose a manufacturer technical URL and most product claims have no visible provenance.

answerEngineExtractability.preventsHigherScore: H1, summary, SKU, price, application, connectivity, specifications, breadcrumbs and links are present in initial HTML. Extractability is reduced by vague summaries, raw specification strings and facts that require comparison rather than a direct answer.

coverage.applicationPageCommonFinding: All 18 pages are useful crawlable catalogues with comparisons and contextual links, but the shared answer is essentially 'browse N products' and the pages do not define the application, explain the buyer problem, distinguish product types, or provide source-grounded selection criteria.
coverage.connectivityPageCommonFinding: All six pages give an early definition, deployment fit, advantage, limitation, products, applications and a primary source. Combined data-bundle pages carefully avoid claiming coverage. They remain descriptive rather than comparative and do not answer LoRaWAN-versus-cellular selection directly.

guidesReviewed.finding: Matches purchase intent and compares 10 products, but the decision criteria are generic and there is no South Africa-specific network/deployment explanation.
Combines useful water categories, but does not distinguish flow, quality and leak-detection jobs deeply enough to guide a choice.

corePagesReviewed.homepage: Clear South African IoT catalogue proposition and useful entry points; WebSite schema only and limited evidence of business identity or topical expertise.
corePagesReviewed.productsIndex: Searchable/filterable catalogue with server-rendered first 24 cards and 50 ItemList entities; the remaining interactive list requires JavaScript, while all product URLs remain independently static and sitemap-discoverable.
corePagesReviewed.compare: Correctly noindex,follow; server-rendered query output supports up to four products in a semantic table and exposes the selected SKUs without client interaction.
corePagesReviewed.about: Clear reseller purpose and enquiry journey, but lacks authoritative legal/business identity, contact details and an explicit LoRa Network-to-Dragino relationship statement. No Organization JSON-LD is present.

consistentStrengths: One exact-SKU H1 per sampled page.
SKU, application, connectivity and price appear near the top of initial HTML.
Product overview uses a definition list; comparisons use a table with a caption and scoped row headers.
All priced samples had identical visible and Offer values; the unpriced AIS01-LS sample displayed Contact for pricing and emitted no Offer.
Canonical, Product, BreadcrumbList and visible Q&A were present on every sampled product page.
consistentWeaknesses: The introductory pattern '[SKU] is a Dragino product for [Application]. It uses [Interface].' rarely explains the physical product or its principal measurement/function.
Manufacturer is not explicitly labelled as manufacturer; the visible field and JSON-LD use Brand: Dragino.
Specifications are one comma-separated paragraph rather than individually named values, which makes model-to-model extraction harder.
Suitability is generally absent. The workbook application label is repeated instead of explaining who should choose the item.
Variant differences are only available indirectly through family comparison tables. In the sample, 12 of 20 pages had no family/compare link and 9 of 20 had no buying-guide link.
Meta descriptions are unique through source values but can be mechanically truncated mid-specification at 155 characters.

entityClarity.intendedRelationshipAssessment: Mostly understandable to a human: LoRa Network is the visible site/reseller brand, Dragino is a product brand, SKUs are products, applications are browse categories and connectivity labels are technologies. Machines lack an explicit Organization entity and explicit reseller/manufacturer relationship.
entityClarity.misrepresentationRisk: LOW to MEDIUM. No page reviewed calls LoRa Network the manufacturer or claims the site is Dragino's official corporate site. However, Product JSON-LD has Brand rather than manufacturer, and the site does not explicitly state the reseller relationship in machine-readable form.

draginoReferenceAudit.renderedTextCounts: Representative extracted HTML contained about four Dragino mentions per product page, two on the homepage, one on the products index and three on About; LoRa Network appeared at least as often in the same samples.
draginoReferenceAudit.marketingStyleReferences: Homepage/about/footer use short phrases such as Dragino hardware or Dragino LoRaWAN and IoT hardware. These are mild catalogue positioning statements, not official-manufacturer claims.
draginoReferenceAudit.legitimateManufacturerReferences: Product summary, visible Brand field, source technical link context and Product JSON-LD brand are legitimate identifiers.
draginoReferenceAudit.structuredDataReferences: Every Product entity uses Brand name Dragino. No Organization or manufacturer entity is emitted.
draginoReferenceAudit.unnecessaryRepetition: The generic product sentence plus visible Brand plus footer repeats Dragino on every product page. This is not severe stuffing, but it adds less value than a richer model-specific definition.

Product.notes: Only used on individual product pages. SKU, brand, category, URL, image when available and source-backed additional properties are emitted.

Offer.notes: Only 969 priced products emit an Offer; priceCurrency is ZAR and price matches visible output. No fake availability, condition, shipping or stock is claimed. Because this is enquiry-led rather than direct checkout, product-snippet rather than full merchant-listing expectations are the safer interpretation.

BreadcrumbList.notes: Present on all products, families and guides. Application and connectivity detail pages render visual breadcrumbs but omit BreadcrumbList JSON-LD.

CollectionPage.notes: Used for catalogue, facets and families. Facet/catalogue ItemLists intentionally cap itemListElement at 50 while declaring the full numberOfItems; this is incomplete rather than a parse error.

ItemList.status: VALID BUT PARTIAL ON LARGE COLLECTIONS
ItemList.notes: ListItem positions and URLs are coherent. The products index initially renders 24 cards while JSON-LD lists 50, creating a modest visible-content alignment concern.

Article.notes: Only the five genuine buying guides use Article. Headline, description and mainEntityOfPage are present; author, publisher, dates and image are absent rather than fabricated.

Organization.notes: This is a material entity/trust gap. It should only be added when legal name, URL, logo and supplied contact/business facts can be stated accurately.

WebSite.notes: Names LoRa Network South Africa and uses the configured site URL. It does not substitute for an Organization entity.

FAQPage.status: VALID JSON-LD, LOW EXPECTED SEARCH VALUE
FAQPage.notes: The questions and answers are visible, but the same template is emitted on 981 commercial product pages. Google limits FAQ rich results largely to authoritative government and health sites; no recommendation is made to add more FAQPage markup merely for AEO.

structuredDataAudit.unsupportedClaimsCheck: No fake availability, ratings, reviews, authors, certifications or merchant policies were found in structured data.
structuredDataAudit.duplicateOrConflictingEntities: No conflicting Product prices or duplicate Product entities were found in the audited product corpus. WebSite and page-level entities are separate and coherent.

priceIntegrity.surfaceAssessment: Cards, product detail, related products, application/connectivity collections, family/guide comparisons and the dynamic compare table all use the central public price presentation. Product Offer values use the same central calculation.

supplierPriceExposure.html: No source-price field names were found in audited public output; reconciliation independently reports zero USD and zero EUR prices publicly exposed.
supplierPriceExposure.jsonAndApi: No public catalogue JSON endpoint exists. The enquiry API does not expose catalogue data. The source catalogue JSON is repository/server data, not under public.
supplierPriceExposure.clientBundles: No priceUsd, usdZarRate, markupRate, supplierPrice, MARKUP_RATE or USD_ZAR_RATE identifiers were found in .next/static.
supplierPriceExposure.staticFiles: No workbook or source catalogue JSON exists under public.
supplierPriceExposure.sourceMaps: No client-side source maps were present under .next/static. Server build source maps are server artifacts, not public assets.
supplierPriceExposure.metadataAndStructuredData: Only public ZAR prices are emitted. The 12 unpriced products emit no Offer.

strengths: Indexable product pages are all in the sitemap and linked through catalogue collections.
Products link to the appropriate indexable application and connectivity facets when those facets exist.
Application pages link to relevant products, connectivity pages and overlapping guides.
Connectivity pages link to relevant products, applications, guides and authoritative technical sources.
Family and guide comparisons use specific product URLs; compare links encode at most four valid slugs and the destination is noindex,follow.
No parameterized search/filter URL crawl trap was found because product catalogue filters are client state, not crawlable URL combinations.
gaps: Only seven family definitions exist, leaving many repeated SKU ranges without a family or comparison link.
Only five guides exist; in the 20-product sample, nine products had no guide link.
In the 20-product sample, 12 pages had no family/compare link, including DDS20/45/75, D22/D23, CS01, AIS01 and RS485W examples.

Products whose source application/interface is outside the curated indexable facet lists display the value without a contextual facet link; this is deliberate index-quality control but creates weaker topical paths for those items.
Repeated anchors such as Technical details, Compare related models and Read the guide are understandable but less descriptive out of context than model/topic-specific anchors.
No broken internal links were observed in source/build route mapping; a full deployed crawler was outside scope because no production URL was provided.
internalLinkGraph.orphanRisk: LOW for products because of sitemap and catalogue inclusion; MEDIUM for topical understanding because many products have only broad application-related links rather than family/guide context.
internalLinkGraph.overlinkingRisk: MEDIUM on very large application/connectivity pages, which render every matching product plus large comparison and related-link sections. The pages are useful but can become link-dense without adding decision hierarchy.

answers.connectivityOptions: PASS through comparison rows and related connectivity links.
answers.whichSuitsWhichUseCase: FAIL/PARTIAL - application labels exist, but variant suitability is not explained.

authoritativeSources.source: GSMA - Mobile IoT in a 5G Future

sourceAndCitationQuality.catalogueProvenance: The supplied workbook is authoritative internally and no unsupported fields are manufactured. However, only 212 of 981 products have a nonblank productUrl, leaving 769 product pages without a visible technical-details source link.
sourceAndCitationQuality.weakSourceFindings: No technical claims based on forums, marketplaces or third-party resellers were found in visible site content. Image provenance records include manufacturer/third-party licensing detail internally, but image sourcing is not presented as technical evidence.
sourceAndCitationQuality.unsourcedAiClaims: No clearly invented AI-style compatibility or certification claims were found. Generic guide advice is cautious but usually uncited.
sourceAndCitationQuality.provenanceRecommendation: Maintain workbook row provenance and attach official manufacturer documentation to products/families when verified; visibly distinguish source facts from reseller guidance. Do not cite secondary resellers when a primary source exists.

strengths: Public prices use South African rand.
The root language is en-ZA and Open Graph locale is en_ZA.
Homepage, About, product price questions and metadata naturally identify the South African market.
The enquiry process avoids unsupported stock, delivery and availability claims.
gaps: VAT treatment is deferred to quotation rather than established site-wide.
No configured public address, phone or email appeared in the audited build.
Guides rarely add South African network, deployment or procurement context.
No supplied shipping, delivery, warranty, returns or local-support facts are available, so the site cannot answer those purchase questions.
southAfricanCommercialRelevance.overuseAssessment: South Africa wording is present in global metadata and repeated template chrome but is not visibly keyword-stuffed.
southAfricanCommercialRelevance.unsupportedClaimAssessment: No unsupported stock, delivery, warranty, certification or local-support promises were found.

searchIntentCoverage.reason: 203 LoRaWAN products, ZAR prices, a sourced technology page and many application links; selection guidance remains a secondary weakness.
Ten gateway products and a buying guide exist, but model-selection and local deployment guidance are thin.
135 direct NB-IoT products plus combined variants, clear ZAR prices and a GSMA-sourced definition.
Flow, quality and leak categories plus a guide provide breadth, but no deep problem-to-product decision path.
The SW3L family has 80 models with pricing and comparison; synthesis of meter/size differences is missing.
Many RS485 converters/nodes exist, but the term gateway may not match the product role and the site does not clarify that distinction.
The RS485/Modbus guide discovers relevant products, but it does not explain protocol compatibility or boundaries.
Large temperature catalogue and a guide are present; model-level measurement and probe decisions need clearer extraction.
Twenty-nine application products and a WQS family exist, but measurement capabilities are buried.
The catalogue is broad and commercially localized, but there is no strong industrial solution narrative or authoritative topic hub.

contentDuplication.productPages: High template repetition is expected for a catalogue, but the unique content often consists only of SKU, application, interface, a raw specification string and price. The repeated 'What is' FAQ answer adds little unique interpretation across 981 pages.
contentDuplication.applicationPages: All 18 use the same count/compare structure and differ mainly by label, products and links. This is useful faceting but weak standalone decision content.
contentDuplication.connectivityPages: Acceptable templating with materially distinct sourced definitions, fits, advantages and limitations. The two data-bundle variants necessarily overlap with their parent technologies and should remain carefully differentiated.
contentDuplication.familyPages: Purpose and answer text often repeat 'compare specification, connectivity, package information and price'; the tables are unique, but narrative value is thin.
contentDuplication.guides: All five repeat four generic comparison criteria and a product table. Their different scopes are legitimate, but editorial differentiation is insufficient.
contentDuplication.riskConclusion: MEDIUM. This is not a doorway-page scheme, but 981 indexable templates with low explanatory uniqueness may struggle to earn citations or strong indexing independently.

indexation.importantContentIndexable: YES, subject to correct production hostname configuration.
indexation.compare: noindex,follow and omitted from sitemap - correct.
indexation.filterAndSearchUrls: No crawlable parameter combinations are generated for catalogue filtering/search - no crawl trap detected.
indexation.apiRoutes: The enquiry API is not in the sitemap and is not an HTML content route.
indexation.canonicalRisk: HIGH before deployment configuration: the audited build emitted http://localhost:3000 in all 981 product canonicals, robots sitemap reference, sitemap URLs and JSON-LD URLs because NEXT_PUBLIC_SITE_URL was unset.
indexation.indexBloatRisk: MEDIUM from indexing all 981 largely templated product pages. Do not blanket-noindex them; first improve unique usefulness and use index-performance evidence to decide if any genuinely non-useful records should be excluded.
indexation.lastModified: All sitemap entries share the fixed catalogue date 2026-09-07, even editorial/legal pages. This is consistent but not a true per-page modification signal.

aiCrawlerStatus.statusMeaning: All standards-compliant crawlers below are allowed through the wildcard rule, but none is explicitly configured. Actual production access can still be affected by WAF/CDN rules that were not available in the repository.

crawlers.implication: Google Search and Google AI features can crawl under the wildcard rule; Google documents Googlebot controls as applying to AI features in Search.
Bing/Microsoft crawl access is not blocked by robots.txt; actual indexing and Copilot citation are not guaranteed.
OpenAI documents GPTBot as a model-training crawler, separate from OAI-SearchBot. This policy should be a deliberate business choice rather than assumed necessary for search visibility.
OpenAI documents it as the crawler used to surface sites in ChatGPT search; wildcard access permits it.
Perplexity documents it as the search-results crawler; wildcard access permits it.
Anthropic identifies this as its model-development crawler; allowing it is distinct from search visibility.
Anthropic identifies this as its search-quality crawler; wildcard access permits it.
Anthropic identifies this as user-directed retrieval; wildcard access does not block it.

aiCrawlerStatus.recommendationBoundary: Do not automatically add explicit allow rules for every crawler. Document the desired search-versus-training policy first, then align robots.txt and WAF rules deliberately.

llmsTxt.assessment: llms.txt is an emerging, non-standard convention and not a guaranteed ranking or citation factor. Its absence is not a crawl blocker.

technicalExtraction.mitigationAlreadyPresent: Each product is a static route and appears in the sitemap; CollectionPage/ItemList JSON-LD provides the first 50 catalogue URLs.
technicalExtraction.interactionDependencyFinding: Core product facts do not require JavaScript or expanding details. Collapsed Q&A remains present in server HTML.

headingsAndSemantics.h1: One clear H1 was found on all inspected page types.
headingsAndSemantics.hierarchy: Product, family, guide, application and connectivity pages generally use logical H2 sections. Card titles use H2 within grids, which can make large collection heading outlines noisy but still understandable.
headingsAndSemantics.tables: Comparison components use a caption, th elements and row scope, supporting extraction and accessibility.
headingsAndSemantics.definitionLists: Product overview, quick facts and package information use dl/dt/dd appropriately.
headingsAndSemantics.landmarks: The root layout provides header, one main wrapper and footer plus a skip link. Privacy and Terms components also return main elements, causing nested main landmarks.
headingsAndSemantics.articles: Guide cards and guide detail content use article semantics appropriately; product content is correctly not presented as editorial Article markup.
headingsAndSemantics.breadcrumbs: Visible breadcrumb navigation exists on product/family/guide/facet pages, but nav elements lack an aria-label and application/connectivity facets lack BreadcrumbList JSON-LD.

citationAdvantages: No fabricated stock, ratings or compatibility
citationDisadvantages: Most product definitions add little beyond manufacturer fields
Application pages are predominantly filtered grids
No direct technology or variant-difference synthesis
competitiveAnswerQuality.likelyCitationOutcome: An answer engine has a credible reason to cite LoRa Network for current ZAR price, catalogue availability and side-by-side factual comparison. It has less reason to cite the site for technical education, suitability or compatibility, where a manufacturer or standards body is more authoritative.

findings.evidence: With NEXT_PUBLIC_SITE_URL unset, the production build emitted http://localhost:3000 in all 981 sampled-corpus product canonicals, JSON-LD URLs, the 1,027 sitemap URLs and robots.txt Sitemap directive.
findings.whyItMatters: If deployed this way, canonical and discovery signals point crawlers away from the public hostname and create a severe indexation/citation problem.
findings.recommendedFix: Set and validate NEXT_PUBLIC_SITE_URL in every production build/deploy environment and add a deployment check that rejects localhost canonicals/sitemap URLs.

findings.evidence: The recurring answer pattern states only that a SKU is a Dragino product for an application and uses an interface; source specifications remain a comma-separated paragraph.
findings.whyItMatters: Answer engines can extract identity and price but often cannot confidently explain what the hardware is, its key function, suitability or differences.
findings.recommendedFix: Using only verified source fields and primary documentation, produce a concise model-specific definition and structured specification labels; preserve unknowns and avoid inferred compatibility.

findings.evidence: Every application page uses the same count/compare answer and then renders a comparison plus product grid; no application-specific definition, buyer problem or selection criteria are present.
findings.whyItMatters: These URLs are useful filters but weak standalone answers, reducing their chance of ranking or being cited for application-level buyer questions.
findings.recommendedFix: Enrich only the existing high-value application pages with short source-grounded definitions, product-type breakdowns and selection criteria. Do not create additional doorway pages.

findings.evidence: No Organization JSON-LD exists, the audited build has no configured public email/phone/address, and no explicit statement defines LoRa Network as reseller and Dragino as manufacturer/brand.
findings.whyItMatters: Weak commercial identity and entity relationships reduce trust and make attribution/citation less confident.
findings.recommendedFix: Once authoritative business details are supplied, add accurate visible identity/contact information and consistent Organization/reseller relationship markup. Do not invent legal or credential data.

findings.evidence: 769 of 981 catalogue products have a blank productUrl; only 212 expose a manufacturer technical-details link.
findings.whyItMatters: Most technical statements lack visible primary-source provenance, weakening trust and making the reseller page less defensible as a citation.
findings.recommendedFix: Reconcile official manufacturer documentation at exact SKU or validated family level and expose verified sources without replacing the workbook as the catalogue authority.

findings.evidence: Guides range from roughly 216 to 848 extracted words including navigation/table text and repeat generic four-step criteria; Article schema contains only headline, description and mainEntityOfPage.
findings.whyItMatters: The guides identify products but only modestly help a buyer make a decision or establish editorial authority.
findings.recommendedFix: Deepen existing guides with verified decision dimensions, limitations and South African context; add author/publisher/date schema only when genuine data and editorial process exist.

findings.evidence: Only seven families are modeled. Repeated high-volume source patterns such as DDS20/45/75, D20/D22/D23, AIS01, CS01 and RS485W lack family paths; 12 of 20 sampled products had no compare link.
findings.whyItMatters: Variant relationships and differences are difficult to extract, despite sufficient catalogue patterns to investigate several high-value families.
findings.recommendedFix: Validate a small prioritized set against official documentation, then improve existing architecture only where a real family and useful comparison can be proven.

findings.evidence: Family purpose text frequently says to compare specification, connectivity, package information and price; tables expose data but do not summarize what differs or which use case fits each option.
findings.whyItMatters: Machines and buyers still have to infer the decisive difference from raw cells.
findings.recommendedFix: Add verified family-purpose, variant-difference and selection summaries to the existing family pages, without inventing compatibility.

findings.evidence: Every product emits a largely templated FAQPage; Google documents that FAQ rich results are generally limited to authoritative government and health sites.
findings.whyItMatters: The markup adds maintenance and duplication without a likely Google rich-result benefit; repetitive answers do not establish authority.
findings.recommendedFix: Keep visible buyer questions where useful, but evaluate structured FAQPage markup on its semantic merits and avoid adding more repetitive FAQs for AEO alone.

findings.evidence: Visible breadcrumbs exist but BreadcrumbList JSON-LD is absent on all facet detail pages; product/family/guide breadcrumbs do have markup.
findings.whyItMatters: The hierarchy is visible but not consistently machine-described.
findings.recommendedFix: Add consistent BreadcrumbList only to existing pages, matching visible navigation and canonical URLs.

findings.evidence: Collection ItemLists cap itemListElement at 50 while numberOfItems reports the full set; /products initially renders 24 cards but its JSON-LD lists 50.
findings.whyItMatters: Large collection entities are incomplete and the initial visible list does not perfectly align with structured items.
findings.recommendedFix: Align visible and marked-up collection subsets or use a more explicit crawlable pagination/collection strategy if future evidence justifies it; do not expose all 981 in one oversized JSON-LD block merely for AEO.

findings.evidence: Product descriptions concatenate generic summaries and raw specs then slice at 155 characters; facet descriptions are minimal count templates.
findings.whyItMatters: Search snippets and answer previews may be unclear, truncated or indistinguishable across variants.
findings.recommendedFix: Generate concise, human-readable, source-backed descriptions around SKU, function, interface and public ZAR availability, without keyword stuffing.

findings.evidence: Rendered/source text contains mojibake such as â€”, modelâ€™s and Â©.
findings.whyItMatters: Encoding artifacts damage professionalism, snippet quality and exact answer text.
findings.recommendedFix: Normalize affected source files to UTF-8 and verify rendered text in a production build.

findings.evidence: RootLayout wraps every route in main, while Privacy and Terms return another main element.
findings.whyItMatters: Nested main landmarks are invalid semantics and can confuse assistive technology and structural extraction.
findings.recommendedFix: Use section/div inside the root main while preserving the same visible layout.

findings.evidence: LoRaWAN, NB-IoT, LTE-M and LTE Cat 1 are explained separately, but no existing page directly compares their deployment trade-offs.
findings.whyItMatters: A high-value buyer question fails manual extraction despite the site already possessing credible primary-source material.
findings.recommendedFix: Add a sourced comparison section to the most appropriate existing guide/index rather than creating multiple keyword pages.

findings.evidence: All bots use a wildcard allow; Googlebot, Bingbot, GPTBot, OAI-SearchBot, PerplexityBot, ClaudeBot and Claude-SearchBot are not named explicitly.
findings.whyItMatters: Access is currently open, but search and training policies are not documented separately and production WAF behaviour remains unknown.
findings.recommendedFix: Make a deliberate business policy decision before adding bot-specific rules; confirm CDN/WAF access and monitor logs.

findings.whyItMatters: This does not block indexing; llms.txt remains an emerging, non-standard discovery convention.
findings.recommendedFix: Optionally add a concise public-content map only after core entity/content gaps are resolved; never include supplier pricing or hidden AI-only copy.

findings.evidence: Every sitemap URL uses the same fixed 2026-09-07 lastModified value, including About, Privacy, Terms and guides.
findings.whyItMatters: The signal does not represent actual per-page editorial updates and may become stale.
findings.recommendedFix: Use truthful source-specific dates when available or omit lastModified where it cannot be maintained accurately.

indexationRisks: Localhost canonical/sitemap/JSON-LD URLs if NEXT_PUBLIC_SITE_URL is not set during production build.
Medium quality/index-bloat risk from 981 indexable product pages with substantial boilerplate and limited model-specific explanations.
Very large application/connectivity pages are link-dense and lack crawlable pagination, although product URLs remain sitemap-discoverable.
Sitemap lastModified dates are not page-specific.
No parameter/filter crawl trap was found; compare is correctly noindex,follow.
structuredDataRisks: Current audited URLs resolve to localhost without production configuration.
FAQPage is repeated on all 981 products with low likely Google rich-result value.
Facet breadcrumbs are visible but not represented by BreadcrumbList.
Article entities are accurate but minimal.
Collection ItemLists are partial on large lists and not perfectly aligned with initially rendered cards.
No fake offers, availability, ratings, reviews or authors were found.
contentGaps: Commercial policy answers when authoritative details become available
topicalAuthorityGaps: Only five short buying guides for a 981-product catalogue.
Application pages mostly function as filters rather than expert topic resources.
Limited primary citations outside connectivity pages.
No synthesized technical comparisons across connectivity or major unmodeled families.
No verified South African network/operator or deployment guidance, which is preferable to inventing it but leaves a local authority gap.
topStrengths: All 981 product pages are statically generated with answer-critical facts in initial HTML.
Public pricing is centralized, ZAR-only and perfectly reconciled across visible/schema surfaces.
Twelve products with blank source prices correctly show Contact for pricing and emit no Offer.
All 981 Product JSON-LD blocks parse; no fake availability, ratings or reviews were found.
Exact SKU values are preserved and clear in H1, overview and structured data.
Application, connectivity, family, guide and related-product pathways form a useful base graph.
All six connectivity pages use cautious, primary-source-backed explanations.
Comparison tables are semantic and expose useful source facts and ZAR prices.
The sitemap is selective, filters do not create crawl traps and compare is correctly noindex,follow.
LoRa Network remains the visible public brand while Dragino is presented as a product brand, with no official-site claim.
topWeaknesses: The audited build emits localhost canonicals, sitemap URLs and JSON-LD URLs without deployment configuration.
Product 'what is' answers are generic and seldom define the actual device.
Specifications are raw comma-separated strings rather than extractable labelled facts.
All 18 application pages are thin filtered catalogues with little decision value.
Business/entity identity is incomplete and Organization structured data is absent.
Only 212 of 981 products provide a visible manufacturer technical-source URL.
Five buying guides are too generic to establish broad topical authority.
Only seven family pages exist; many obvious variant ranges have no comparison path.
Variant difference and suitability answers are usually implicit or absent.
Mojibake, templated metadata and repeated FAQ answers reduce editorial quality.

Reject repetitive FAQ expansion and FAQPage markup added only for rich-result hopes.
Reject fake reviews, ratings, authors, credentials or editorial dates.
Reject unsupported stock, delivery, warranty, compatibility, certification and network-coverage claims.
Reject South African location doorway pages.
Reject manufacturer-name stuffing or wording that implies LoRa Network is Dragino's official corporate site.

Reject duplicate category pages for keyword variants.
Every AEO improvement should make a real buyer's decision easier.

recommendedNextActions.action: Set the production public site URL and add a deployment assertion that fails on localhost canonical, sitemap, robots or JSON-LD URLs.
Add accurate visible business identity and contact details, then implement a consistent Organization/reseller relationship only from supplied authoritative facts.
Create a source-governed product-answer model that turns verified workbook/manufacturer facts into a concise definition and labelled specifications without inferring compatibility.

Prioritize the highest-value existing application pages (distance, temperature, water flow, smart agriculture, pressure) for definitions, buyer problems, product types and verified selection criteria.
Reconcile primary manufacturer documentation for products currently lacking technical source links, starting with high-traffic/high-value families.
Deepen the five existing guides with sourced decision dimensions, limitations, comparison interpretation and legitimate South African context.
Validate and add only a small number of obvious high-value missing families, beginning with DDS distance ranges and temperature ranges; do not generate pages from prefixes alone.
Add concise, verified variant-difference and suitability summaries to the seven existing family pages and relevant product pages.
Resolve UTF-8 mojibake, improve programmatic metadata quality, remove nested main landmarks and align visible breadcrumbs/ItemLists with structured data.
Document a deliberate AI search-versus-training crawler policy, verify CDN/WAF access, and only then consider explicit robots entries or a minimal llms.txt content map.
